value.title: Access Control Header Mutation & 403 Response Differential
value.content: {"id": "recon_meth_011", "item_type": "methodology", "topic": "recon", "name": "Access Control Header Mutation & 403 Response Differential", "prerequisites": ["reverse_proxy_mechanics", "http_headers"], "signals": ["forbidden_403_status", "x_forwarded_for_bypass", "x_original_url_rewrite", "path_normalization_traversal"], "verification_strategy": "Test restricted endpoints (HTTP 403) by mutating proxy forwarding headers (X-Forwarded-For: 127.0.0.1, X-Original-URL, X-Rewrite-URL) and applying path normalization tricks (e.g. /admin/./ or /admin%20) to evaluate whether frontend reverse proxy rules desynchronize from backend access logic.", "evidence_requirements": ["status_differential_403_to_200", "authorized_response_body_hash"], "remediation_pattern": "Enforce authorization logic at the application controller level rather than relying solely on reverse proxy URL filtering rules. Strip untrusted client-supplied forwarding headers at the edge proxy.", "description": "Evaluating discrepancies between reverse proxies and application backends where header manipulation or path normalization allows unauthorized access to restricted interfaces."}
